what: Five blur layers (3·4.5·9·24·75px, stronger toward the bottom, with the mask starting 12.5% later each) sit in an 18rem strip at the bottom of the screen. Scroll speed × .011~.003 per layer builds up each layer’s opacity, up to .55·.35·.22·.16·.05 (the lightest blur layer gets the darkest). The faster you scroll, the more the text below smears, when you stop, it clears after 150ms with a .8s easeOut.

options.bottom: Offset below the strip (e.g. bar height under the phone), default 0
options.gain: Speed multiplier (applied to all layers), default 1
options.settle: Wait after stopping before it clears (ms), default 150

note: Speed uses lenis.velocity (as in the original) if window.lenis exists, otherwise the per-frame window scroll difference (px). It is a backdrop-filter, so text·photos beneath the panel are blurred — clicks pass straight through.
